Measured real-time factor of the default (wall time / audio time; 2 threads, int8, nice 19, load average 4-7):

| Audio | Speech share | RTF |
|---|---|---|
| Prague tower set, 600 s | 64 % | 0.38 |
| Prague sample, 145 s, three runs | 72 % | 0.35-0.47 |
| US tower sample, 196 s | 29 % | 0.17 |
| US tower set, 3,499 s | 10.5 % | 0.10 |

That is 0.5-0.9 s of computing per second of speech, plus 7-8 s for each transmission the second look re-reads. A 30-minute block should take roughly 5-14 minutes; --second-opinion costs about 2.2 times that.

Why this model:

| Model | Prague set (human transcripts): WER, callsigns found of 13 | US tower set (weak ADS-B labels): airline-type callsign mentions |
|---|---|---|
| large-v3-turbo | 0.45, 5 | 13 |
| ATC fine-tune | 0.21, 11 | 5 |
| small.en | 0.59, 2 | 10 |

Turbo is best on US phraseology, which is what SFO is. The fine-tune is far better on its home ground but turns US telephony into European airline names. Both sets are small.

Self-test (find_calls.py --self-test: 61 text cases plus two real samples, clips included; 2 min 50 s):

| Model set | Prague sample: of 8 human-transcribed calls, covered at conf >= 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.8 | False hits | US sample: of 3 calls, covered at >= 0.3 / 0.5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| default | 8 / 5 / 2 | 0 | 3 / 0 |
| --second-opinion | 8 / 8 / 8 | 0 | 3 / 0 |
| --fast | 6 / 2 / 0 | 0 | 3 / 0 |

- The default alone finds every call, but half only as a bare number at 0.30-0.35 because it garbles the airline name. Low-confidence rows are candidates to listen to, so the final cut list should come from --second-opinion.
- The US sample's reference is silver: it comes from the default model's own output, as no human transcript exists.
- All 14 clips measure -23.1 LUFS, true peak -2.3 dBTP or lower, and an independent BS.1770-4 computation agrees.

Four things in the tool differ from what you might assume:
- **ffmpeg's loudnorm filter is not used**, although the brief named it. On 4-9 s clips its second pass left linear mode (a clip came out at -21.25 LUFS for -23) and its own meter read 0.4-0.9 LU low against two other meters. The tool measures with ffmpeg's ebur128 meter and applies one constant gain, with a limiter only for peaks.
- **Energy gate instead of Silero VAD**: the VAD kept 0.9 s of about 50 s of real tower speech.
- **No prompt by default**: the ATC prompt cost airline names (2 of 13 callsigns instead of 5).
- **Second look**: every transmission with the callsign is transcribed again on its own, and a miss halves the confidence. This was added because the ATC fine-tune wrote the target callsign over another aircraft's call. It is a warning, not a verdict: turbo failed to re-hear 1 of 10 real calls, and small.en 3 of 3 on the US sample, so --fast skips it.

(2) Any scripted fetch or stream recording by the session: forbidden by 3.13, no access "with any program, collection agent, or "robot" for the purpose of automated retrieval of content, unless you are granted permission by LiveATC.net to do so". (3) A film for the owner's own viewing with the credit "ATC audio: LiveATC.net": INFERRED to fit 2.1 ("for personal non-commercial purposes only") and 3.2 (no copying, storing or editing "without giving credit to LiveATC.net as the source of the original material"); LiveATC has not said so, and 3.7 ("create derivative works based on the LiveATC.net Services or any portion of them") can be read against any edited film. (4) Showing or posting the film, monetised or not: not permitted by the written terms unless LiveATC agrees - 2.1 ends "ANY USE OF THE LIVEATC.NET SERVICES NOT SPECIFICALLY PERMITTED UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IS STRICTLY PROHIBITED.", summary point 2 bars use "for personal gain, financial or otherwise", and the founder wrote on LiveATC's forum on 12 Apr 2023 (capture 2025-07-14) "If you are using audio in YT or other videos and monetizing it you need to contact us via the contact page." Retention, "Archives are available for 7 days" and "older than 7 days (but less than 1 year old) ... fee will apply": FIRSTHAND as of the captures of 2025-10-10 and 2025-12-10 of https://www.liveatc.net/archive.php.
